commands.reason: Measured on 8 November 2026 (#1681) at 159: every relish command and subcommand at every depth, none of them hidden. Raised to 161 for #1685: `relish timeline` for people and `relish agent timeline` for agents, the incident timeline. Raised by 2 more for #1689: `relish verify` for people and `relish agent verify` for agents, one check of the cluster against the published release. Raised by 5 more for #1683: `relish gym`, `gym run` and `gym list`, plus the hidden `gym record` and `gym baseline` that `gym run` starts for the solver. Raised by 10 for #1686, which adds leases between agents: `relish lease` (list, take, renew, release, break) for people and `relish agent lease` (take, renew, release) for agents, as the 0.2.8 design specifies. Raised by 10 for #1682's proposals: `relish proposal` (list, show, approve, reject) and `relish undo` for people, and `relish agent propose`, `proposals`, `withdraw` and `undo` for agents, as the design specifies (propose takes the kind as an argument rather than five subcommands, to keep the count down). Raised by 1 for `relish apps` (#1777): the lists left `relish status`, which became one screen of counts

flags.reason: Measured on 8 November 2026 (#1681) at 375: named flags on every command, global ones once. Raised to 390 for #1685: the two timeline commands' window and scope flags, and `relish agent explain`'s --restart, --placement, --refusal and --rules, which ask why the cluster made a decision. Raised by 8 more for #1689: `relish verify` and `relish agent verify` each take --release-url, --metadata, --cli-metadata and --artefacts, so a check can run offline against files on disk. Raised by 10 more for #1683: `relish gym run`'s nine flags (the staging namespace, solver, scenarios, runs, timeout, output directory, image and the two consents) and `gym record`'s --log. Raised by 14 for #1686's lease commands (the target's --namespace, --purpose, --ttl/--for and --wait). Raised by 13 for #1682: `--yes` on `relish proposal approve` and `relish undo`, `--reason` on reject, `relish agent propose`'s --replicas, --namespace, --reason, --ttl, --idempotency-key and --dry-run, `relish agent undo`'s --reason and --ttl, and `relish token create`'s --agent and --ttl. Raised by 6 for #1686's enforcement half: --break-lease on apply, deploy, stop, delete, rollback and release. Raised by 7 for #1777: `status --quick --check`, `apps --namespace --unhealthy --node --instances` and `nodes --unhealthy`, the filters a long list needs. Raised by 2 for #1682's guardrails: `relish mcp --propose`, which offers the proposing tools with a deployer agent token, and `relish policy test --proposal`, which tests a guardrail on a proposal before it's trusted, as the design specifies. Raised by 1 for #1687: `relish mcp --max-bytes`, the server-wide budget a small local model's window needs; it reuses the name `relish agent` already has, so distinct flags don't move. Raised by 1 for #1687: `relish agent guide --section`, which reads one section of the agent guide when a small budget gets its outline. Raised by 2 for #1682's audit, as the design specifies: `relish audit --principal-kind` (what agents did) and `--proposal` (everything one proposal wrote)
